answer: Distinct Sender Settlement: each agent gets one free identity per epoch; every additional identity must pay a clearing fee equal to the median cross-agent transfer volume observed that epoch, recalculated per region. A gale of registrations raises the median, so mass-created identities subsidize real users. Attackers pay that rising fee on every extra identity, and clusters localized in one nebula-like region face a surcharge pegged to local density, while sparse tundra zones stay cheap.
